name: mcom-coculture
title: MCoM co-culture: a phytoplankton bloom feeds a heterotroph
question:
In a closed (batch) box seeded with a single phytoplankton and a single
heterotroph population, does the MCoM reproduction produce the canonical
phototroph-heterotroph succession -- a phytoplankton bloom that draws down
inorganic nitrogen and, through its exuded dissolved organic carbon and
nitrogen, fuels the growth of a heterotroph that would otherwise have almost
no substrate?
hypothesis:
Starting from a tiny heterotroph inoculum (H_init = 0.003, ~1/1000 of the
phytoplankton's carbon) with no external organic supply, the heterotroph can
only grow on carbon and nitrogen the phytoplankton releases. So the
heterotroph population should stay near zero until the phytoplankton bloom
produces DOC/DON, then rise steeply, lagging the bloom; and the inorganic
nitrogen, with no external resupply (D = 0), should be drawn down from its
initial 8.8 mM as the bloom fixes it into biomass.
objective:
Run the `mcom_coculture` composite (the shipped MCoM `configs/test.toml`
parameter set: 1 phytoplankton, 1 heterotroph, a labile + a recalcitrant
DOC/DON pool, constant light, closed box) for 200 days and verify (a) the
heterotroph establishes a substantial population it could only reach by
consuming phytoplankton exudate, and (b) inorganic nitrogen is drawn down.
description:
Wraps the `viva_mcom.composites.coculture.mcom_coculture` generator -- a
single `MComReproductionProcess` carrying the whole community. The parameter
set is MCoM's shipped `configs/test.toml`: a Platt P-I phytoplankton
(use_PI_curve, no light-limited exudation) releasing all its labile carbon to
DOC0 and nitrogen to DON0, and a heterotroph that takes up only the labile
DOC0/DON0 (upDOCH=[[1]], upDONH=[[1]]) while its mortality routes a small
fraction (1%) of carbon to a recalcitrant DOC1 pool that nothing consumes.
The community is a clean-room NumPy reproduction of MCoM's Julia engine
(bit-for-bit against upstream golden data -- see `tests/test_golden.py`), so
the succession below is MCoM's own dynamics, not an approximation.

Achieved (200-day run): the phytoplankton blooms from 0.01 to a peak of ~0.84
(1e6 cells/mL) around day 44, then busts as nitrogen runs out; the heterotroph
rises from 0.003 to a peak ~2.39 around day 50 -- lagging the bloom by ~6 days,
the exudate-consumption signature -- and settles near 0.58; inorganic nitrogen
falls from 8.8 mM to below 0.5 mM, with a second-half mean ~1.87 mM. The
labile DOC0 stays low (consumed) while the recalcitrant DOC1 accumulates.

expected_behavior.name: heterotroph-blooms-on-exudate
expected_behavior.en: The heterotroph, seeded at 0.003 with no external substrate, grows to a substantial population (mean total density over the run > 0.1) it could only reach by consuming phytoplankton-derived DOC/DON.
expected_behavior.rationale: The heterotroph starts at 0.003 (1e6 cells/mL) and has no external organic carbon or nitrogen source (closed box, DOC/DON come only from the phytoplankton). A run-mean total density above 0.1 -- more than 30x the inoculum -- can only arise from growth on exuded DOC/DON, i.e. genuine phototroph->heterotroph coupling. The achieved mean is 0.74; 0.1 sits well above the ~0.003 no-growth floor and well below the achieved value.

expected_behavior.name: inorganic-nitrogen-drawn-down
expected_behavior.en: Inorganic nitrogen is drawn down by the bloom: its mean over the second half of the run falls below 4.0 mM, from an initial 8.8 mM.
expected_behavior.rationale: With no external nitrogen resupply (D = 0), the only sink for inorganic nitrogen is uptake into phytoplankton biomass. A second-half mean below 4.0 mM (from 8.8 mM initial) evidences substantial biological drawdown. The achieved second-half mean is 1.87 mM; 4.0 leaves headroom while still failing a community that never took up nitrogen (which would stay near 8.8).

behavior_tests.name: heterotroph-blooms-on-exudate
behavior_tests.description:
Mean total heterotroph density over the full run exceeds 0.1 (1e6 cells/mL)
-- >30x the 0.003 inoculum, reachable only by consuming phytoplankton exudate.

provenance.note: Heterotroph inoculum is 0.003 with no external substrate; achieved run mean is 0.74. 0.1 sits >30x above the no-growth floor and ~7x below the achieved value -- cleanly separating "grew on exudate" from "did not grow".

behavior_tests.name: inorganic-nitrogen-drawn-down
behavior_tests.description:
Mean inorganic nitrogen over the second half of the run is below 4.0 mM,
down from the initial 8.8 mM -- biological drawdown by the bloom.

provenance.note: Closed box (D=0), so uptake into biomass is the only N sink; achieved second-half mean is 1.87 mM from 8.8 mM initial. 4.0 fails a non-consuming community (stays ~8.8) with headroom over the achieved value.

embed_visualizations.name: succession
embed_visualizations.description: Phytoplankton + heterotroph (log axis) vs inorganic nitrogen -- the bloom-bust succession; the heterotroph peak (2.39 @ day 50) lags the phytoplankton bloom (0.84 @ day 44) by ~7 days, the exudate-consumption signature.

embed_visualizations.name: organic-pools
embed_visualizations.description: Dissolved organic pools: the labile DOC0/DON0 stay low (consumed by the heterotroph) while the recalcitrant DOC1 accumulates from heterotroph mortality.

conclusion:
Both behaviour tests pass. The phytoplankton blooms (0.01 -> 0.84 @ day 44)
and busts; the heterotroph rises on the exuded DOC/DON to a peak of 2.39 @ day
50 -- a ~7-day lag behind the bloom, for a run-mean density of 0.74 (>200x its
0.003 inoculum), which it could only reach by consuming phytoplankton exudate.
Inorganic nitrogen is drawn down from 8.8 mM to a second-half mean of 1.87 mM.
The canonical phototroph-heterotroph batch succession is reproduced.
